A.explanation: Although $E_0$ is across PQ, the $E_X$ loop is connected with the wrong polarity at P so its p.d. cannot oppose the wire p.d. and no null can be found.

B.explanation: The small unknown $E_X$ is used as the driver across PQ while the larger $E_0$ is in the J loop, so $E_0$ exceeds the maximum wire p.d. and balance lies beyond Q.

C.explanation: The galvanometer is in series with $E_0$ in the driver loop, not in series with $E_X$ in the sliding J loop, so it cannot detect zero current in the test cell branch.

D.explanation: The known $E_0$ drives uniform current in PQ and the $E_X$ plus galvanometer loop between P and J opposes the wire p.d., giving a null within the wire because $E_X$ is less than $E_0$.

hints: Notice which cell is connected directly across the ends P and Q of the uniform wire - the driver must be the known $E_0$ because $E_X$ is less than $E_0$.
Check which loop contains the galvanometer with the sliding contact J - the null detector must be in series with the test cell $E_X$, not in the fixed driver loop.
Check that the two positive terminals meet at the same end P so the wire p.d. from P to J can oppose $E_X$ and fall to zero at some position of J inside PQ.
walkthrough: Identify the potentiometer principle: the driver cell maintains a uniform p.d. along wire PQ, and the test cell $E_X$ is connected between one end and the slider J with a galvanometer to find zero current.
The maximum p.d. available on the wire is set by the driver. Since $E_X$ is less than $E_0$, the driver must be $E_0$ connected across P to Q, eliminating the circuit that puts $E_X$ across PQ.
The galvanometer must be in the $E_X$ and J branch so balance is detected as zero test-cell current. This eliminates the circuit that puts the meter in series with $E_0$.
For a null, $E_X$ must oppose the P to J p.d. This requires the like terminals of $E_0$ and $E_X$ to be joined at P, so moving J from P toward Q increases the opposing wire p.d. from zero to $E_0$.
Because $E_X < E_0$, the opposing p.d. equals $E_X$ at a point J inside the known length PQ, allowing $E_X$ to be found from the balance length ratio.
Only the circuit with $E_0$ across PQ and the $E_X$-galvanometer branch from P to J with opposing polarity satisfies all conditions. This is option D.
